Definition: from G5259 and G5021; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey:--be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.
BiblicalUsage: hypotássō turns up where the Bible says to put under, to be subject, to obey. In Luke 2:51, the text says "and was subject unto them." In Romans 8:7, the text says "for it is not subject to the law of God."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hypotássō to mean that obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
